implementations.bs1770: pyloudnorm 0.2.0 (K-weighting filter, loudness range); listener 0.1.0 (gating on complete blocks, 0.4 s and 3 s windows, true peak, spans)
implementations.iso532_1: MoSQITo 1.2.1 loudness_zwtv stages (ISO 532-1:2017 time-varying, free field)
implementations.din45692: MoSQITo 1.2.1 sharpness_din_from_loudness on the ISO 532-1 specific loudness

rule: Each value: dB by which a measure would raise sound B to make it as loud as sound A. 'agrees': within 1 dB of the published range (or the right sign, at least 0.5 dB); 'near': within 3 dB; 'off': further; 'no effect': under 0.5 dB where a sign is expected; 'opposite': the wrong sign.
caution: Stimuli are rebuilt from descriptions; the published ranges come from small panels. This constrains a model. It does not validate one for sound effects.

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, 1 kHz tone, moderate level
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms tone must be raised to match the 200 ms tone
phenomena.reconstruction: both tones at 56 dB SPL before matching; 1 ms raised-cosine ramps

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, 1 kHz tone, high level
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms tone must be raised
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996): about 10 dB near 100 dB SPL
phenomena.reconstruction: both tones at 100 dB SPL; 'about 10 dB' taken as 9 to 11

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, broadband noise, moderate level
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms noise must be raised
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996): 18-19 dB near 76 dB SPL for noise
phenomena.reconstruction: noise 20 Hz to 20 kHz at 76 dB SPL; 1 ms ramps

phenomena.title: Temporal integration, broadband noise, high level
phenomena.question: dB the 5 ms noise must be raised
phenomena.source: Florentine, Buus & Poulsen (1996): about 13 dB near 100 dB SPL for noise
phenomena.reconstruction: noise at 100 dB SPL; 'about 13 dB' taken as 12 to 14

phenomena.title: A rising tone is louder than the same tone falling
phenomena.question: dB the falling tone must be raised to match the rising one
phenomena.source: Ponsot, Susini & Meunier (2015), Atten. Percept. Psychophys. 77(3):907-920; 10 to 16 listeners, two methods
phenomena.reconstruction: 1 kHz, 2 s, 60 to 75 dB SPL linear in dB (the paper used 15 dB ramps within 45-90 dB SPL)

phenomena.title: An impact-like envelope is softer than its time reverse (tone)
phenomena.question: dB the reversed (slow attack, fast decay) sound must be lowered to match the impact-like one
phenomena.source: Stecker & Hafter (2000), JASA 107(6):3358-3368; 250 ms envelopes of equal energy; about 1-3 dB for one listener
phenomena.evidence: single study; the sign is the finding, the size is weak
phenomena.reconstruction: 2 ms attack, exponential decay of 40 dB over 250 ms; the paper's time constants were not available

phenomena.title: An impact-like envelope is softer than its time reverse (noise)
phenomena.question: dB the reversed (slow attack, fast decay) sound must be lowered to match the impact-like one
phenomena.source: Stecker & Hafter (2000), JASA 107(6):3358-3368; 250 ms envelopes of equal energy; about 1-3 dB for one listener
phenomena.evidence: single study; the sign is the finding, the size is weak
phenomena.reconstruction: 2 ms attack, exponential decay of 40 dB over 250 ms; the paper's time constants were not available

phenomena.title: A slow train of impulses is as loud as one impulse
phenomena.question: dB the train must be raised to match the single impulse (none)
phenomena.source: Ogura, Suzuki & Sone (1991), J. Acoust. Soc. Jpn (E) 12(1):1-11: no change up to 0.2-0.7 impulses a second
phenomena.reconstruction: noise impulse of 50 ms, three of them 4 s apart (0.25 a second); 'as loud' taken as within 1 dB

phenomena.title: A fast train of impulses is louder than one impulse
phenomena.question: dB the train must be lowered to match the single impulse
phenomena.source: Ogura, Suzuki & Sone (1991): above the critical rate loudness grows with rate
phenomena.reconstruction: the same impulse, ten of them 0.2 s apart (5 a second)

phenomena.title: A 63 Hz octave band of noise against a 1 kHz band
phenomena.question: dB the 63 Hz band must be raised to match the 1 kHz band
phenomena.source: Fenton & Lee (2017), AES 143rd Convention: listeners gave 9.98 dB where BS.1770 gives 2.73; 13 listeners, loudspeakers
phenomena.reconstruction: octave bands of pink noise, both at 75 dB SPL; 9.98 dB taken as 9 to 11

phenomena.title: A louder beginning counts for more than a louder middle
phenomena.question: dB the sound with the louder middle must be raised to match the one with the louder beginning
phenomena.source: Fischenich, Hots, Verhey, Guldan & Oberfeld (2021), PLoS ONE 16(12):e0261001: onset weight 4-5 times the later weight, time constant 200-300 ms
phenomena.reconstruction: 1 s noise at 65 dB SPL, 6 dB more in the first 100 ms or from 500 to 600 ms

phenomena.title: The same impact dry and with a 2 s reverberant tail
phenomena.question: dB the wet version would be raised (negative: lowered) to match the dry one
phenomena.reconstruction: noise impact of 0.3 s; tail 12 dB under its peak, decaying 60 dB in 2 s

phenomena.title: A 30-150 Hz boom against a 2-6 kHz click, around 60 dB SPL
phenomena.question: dB the boom would be raised to match the click
phenomena.reconstruction: click 30 ms; boom 1.2 s with a 250 ms decay; both built from noise of the stated level

phenomena.title: A 30-150 Hz boom against a 2-6 kHz click, around 80 dB SPL
phenomena.question: dB the boom would be raised to match the click
phenomena.reconstruction: click 30 ms; boom 1.2 s with a 250 ms decay; both built from noise of the stated level
